_comment: Pre-gate screening criteria for the `sdlc` skill, expressed as TypeSafe questions.
Each gate mirrors the written criteria of one SDLC stage. Edit the thresholds here;
the raw judgments stay reusable when a threshold moves. Stage 6 (Maintain) is absent
on purpose: its detector must stay deterministic (bands.yaml sigma), no model in it.
Rules: '<qid> <op> <value>' with op in < <= > >= == != in. 'in' takes a comma list.

plan.title: Plan gate -- is intent.md ready for the human to approve?

problem_distinct.instructions: Does `intent_md` state the problem separately from any proposed solution, rather than opening with an implementation already chosen?

criteria.true: The problem is described on its own terms before any solution is proposed
criteria.false: The document presents an implementation as the starting point, with no problem stated independently of it

constraints_falsifiable.instructions: Are the constraints in `intent_md` stated so that one could later check whether they were respected?

criteria.true: Constraints name concrete limits, systems, or conditions that can be checked against a result
criteria.false: Constraints are aspirational or vague, with nothing checkable in them

open_questions_real.instructions: Are the items `intent_md` lists as open questions genuinely still undecided elsewhere in the same document?

criteria.true: Every listed open question is still unresolved in the document
criteria.false: At least one listed open question is in fact already decided elsewhere in the document

readiness.instructions: Judge how ready this intent is for the human to approve it and start Design.
criteria: no coherent intent yet; needs a rewrite
the shape is there, but the problem or the outcome is still unclear
approvable once a few specific points are confirmed
ready to approve as written

blockers.say: the problem is not stated separately from the solution
listed open questions appear already decided in the document

design.title: Design gate -- does spec.md answer intent.md?

covers_intent.instructions: Does `spec_md` address every outcome proposed in `intent_md`? Answer about coverage of the proposed outcomes only, not about quality.

criteria.true: Every proposed outcome in the intent has corresponding treatment in the spec
criteria.false: At least one proposed outcome in the intent is absent from the spec

narrowing_is_explicit.instructions: If `spec_md` covers less than `intent_md` proposed, does it say so explicitly and name what was deferred? Answer true if the spec covers everything and nothing was deferred.

criteria.true: Either nothing was deferred, or the spec names what it defers and why
criteria.false: The spec quietly omits something the intent proposed, without acknowledging it

has_open_concerns.instructions: Does `spec_md` still contain unresolved areas of concern -- inline `> CONCERN:` blocks, explicit open questions, or decisions deferred to later?

criteria.true: The spec flags at least one concern or open question as unresolved
criteria.false: The spec records no unresolved concerns or open questions

scope_relation.instructions: How does the scope of `spec_md` relate to the scope of `intent_md`?

criteria.faithful: The spec covers the intent's scope, neither adding nor dropping substance
criteria.narrowed: The spec deliberately covers less than the intent proposed
criteria.expanded: The spec introduces substantial scope the intent did not propose
criteria.diverged: The spec pursues a different outcome than the intent asked for

needs_attention.instructions: Which single area of `spec_md` most needs the human's attention before Build starts? Judge by risk of costly rework, not by section length.

criteria.architecture: How the components compose and where the boundaries fall
criteria.verification: How the result will be proven to work
criteria.scope: What is in and out, and what was deferred
criteria.dependencies: Reliance on external systems, other repos, or unfinished work
criteria.none: No area stands out as needing attention before Build

target_quantifiability.instructions: The SDLC requires verification targets to be quantifiable ('all tests in test/x.sh pass') and never subjective ('looks good'). How quantifiable are the verification targets stated in `spec_md`?
criteria: no verification targets are stated at all
targets are stated only in subjective terms
some targets are measurable, others are subjective
every stated target names a concrete, checkable outcome

readiness.instructions: Judge how ready this spec is for the human to accept it and start Build.
criteria: needs a rewrite before review is worthwhile
reviewable, but several substantive gaps must be closed first
acceptable once a few specific points are confirmed
ready to accept as written

blockers.say: the spec appears to narrow the intent without saying so
spec scope has drifted from the intent
verification targets are not quantifiable enough

build.title: Build gate -- is plan.md approvable before code is written?

names_files.instructions: Does `plan_md` name the specific files that will change?

criteria.false: Changes are described only in general terms, with no files named

names_proof_tests.instructions: Does `plan_md` state the proof tests -- how the finished work will be shown to work?

criteria.true: The plan names the tests, commands, or checks that will prove the work
criteria.false: The plan describes what to build but not how it will be proven

ordering_present.instructions: Does `plan_md` give an order of work, rather than an unordered list of changes?

criteria.true: The plan sequences the work, or its steps are meaningfully ordered
criteria.false: The plan is an unordered collection of changes

serves_spec.instructions: Does the work described in `plan_md` implement what `spec_md` specified?

criteria.true: The plan's work follows from the spec
criteria.false: The plan pursues work the spec did not call for, or omits what it did

risk_level.instructions: How much scrutiny does this plan warrant from the human before code is written? Judge by blast radius and reversibility, not by size.

criteria.routine: Reversible, contained, and touches nothing protected
criteria.notable: Touches shared interfaces, data shapes, or several components at once
criteria.high: Irreversible, touches production, credentials, protected paths, or data migration

readiness.instructions: Judge how ready this plan is for the human to approve it and let code be written.
criteria: not a plan yet; needs to be written properly
a sketch; the files or the proof are missing
approvable once a few specific points are confirmed
ready to approve as written

blockers.say: the plan does not state its proof tests
the plan does not name the files that change
the plan does not follow from the spec

test.title: Test gate -- is the claimed proof actually proof?

evidence_present.instructions: Does `report_md` contain actual verification output -- a pasted test log, build output, or command result -- rather than only a description of testing that was done?

criteria.true: Real output is pasted into the report
criteria.false: The report only asserts that verification happened, without showing output

claims_match_evidence.instructions: Do the claims made in `report_md` match the verification output it shows? Answer false if the report claims success the pasted output does not demonstrate.

criteria.true: Every claim is supported by the output shown
criteria.false: At least one claim goes beyond, or contradicts, the output shown

failures_disclosed.instructions: If the verification output contains failures, errors, or skipped work, does `report_md` acknowledge them? Answer true if the output shows no failures at all.

criteria.true: Either the output is clean, or the report acknowledges every failure in it
criteria.false: The output contains failures, errors, or skips that the report does not mention

target_quantifiability.instructions: The SDLC requires verification targets to be quantifiable ('all tests in test/x.sh pass') and never subjective ('looks good'). How quantifiable are the targets this report claims to have met?
criteria: no target is stated; the report only describes activity
the target is subjective, such as 'works' or 'looks good'
some targets are measurable, others are subjective
every target named is concrete and checkable against the output shown

blockers.say: no verification output is shown, only a claim that testing happened
claims go beyond the evidence shown
the output appears to contain failures the report does not mention
the target is subjective; the SDLC requires a quantified one

deploy.title: Deploy gate -- did the review actually happen, and is anything left open?

passes_covered.instructions: Do the findings in `findings` show that every review pass defined in `review_md` was actually run?

criteria.true: Every pass defined in REVIEW.md is represented in the findings
criteria.false: At least one defined pass has no evidence of having been run

unresolved_findings.instructions: Do `findings` contain any finding that is still unresolved -- neither fixed nor explicitly accepted with a reason?

criteria.true: At least one finding is left open with no fix and no stated acceptance
criteria.false: Every finding is either fixed or explicitly accepted with a reason

self_approval.instructions: Do `findings` indicate that the same agent or person who wrote the change also approved it? The SDLC forbids this (separation of duties).

criteria.true: The author of the change appears to have approved their own work
criteria.false: Approval came from someone or something other than the author

highest_severity.instructions: How severe is the most serious unresolved issue in `findings`?
criteria: nothing unresolved
cosmetic or stylistic only
a real defect in a contained area
affects correctness broadly, security, or data integrity

blockers.say: the author appears to have approved their own change (separation of duties)
not every review pass defined in REVIEW.md was run
an unresolved finding is more than cosmetic
